articles.title: Do we really ‘hold tension’ in our hips?
articles.summary: The idea is popular in wellness circles, but experts say there’s no evidence that trauma uniquely affects the hips. Here’s what causes hip tightness and what can help. In yoga classes, on TikTok and throughout other wellness spaces, you’ve probably heard the saying: your hips hold tension.
body: Pain and muscle tension hit harder when you’re going through a difficult time. But should tight hips make you question your mental health? And what can you do to reduce hip tightness? Here’s what you need to know.
When you sense muscle tension in your body, it’s probably caused by one of two things.

The first possibility is not clearly related to stress and involves muscles resisting stretch even when they’re relaxed. Stiffness like this is a mechanical property that reflects how your tissues are built and used.
The other possibility is that your muscles and nerves are engaged in some low-level activity more often than they need to be; this does often happen when people are under psychological stress.
points: The idea is popular in wellness circles, but experts say there’s no evidence that trauma uniquely affects the hips.
Here’s what causes hip tightness and what can help.

articles.title: What’s my first decision as CEO? I’m giving myself the day off | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: A life coach has helpfully pointed out that we’re all chief executives of our own existence. So let’s start enjoying the perks. To-do lists are done, apparently: the latest tactic to motivate and galvanise yourself is a “CEO hour”.
body: Katzler is against the to-do list because she sees it as “our fast track to feeling like we’re completely out of control, because we can never get through it. When you never get that sense of achievement, what you’re left with is a feeling of failure.”

Instead she suggests asking yourself what your wins were from the last week, which tasks you’ve been avoiding, and how you’re managing your energy, time and workload. Also, noting any eureka moments you had, how well you took care of yourself, and what support you need.

Scoff all you like, but for me even the idea of a CEO hour was impactful, because I noticed that my immediate instincts were to wonder how low the bar was for what constituted a win of the week (does “lived to tell the tale” count?) and worry about a boardroom coup. My company felt much more unfortunate Apprentice candidate than Fortune 500.

articles.title: 'Straight out of a loveless, passion-free factory from Protein Inc': the best (and worst) protein powders
articles.summary: Whey protein powder is everywhere, but which ones will you savor and which will you choke down? The Guardian staff glugged them all so you don’t have to. The best (and worst) instant coffee, protein bar or chocolate bars.
body: Proteinmaxxing has gotten out of hand. It’s in everything from ice-cream to yogurt – yes, our protein has extra protein in it now. GLP-1 weight loss drugs are in part to blame; as Americans eat less overall, protein intake becomes more essential. And whey protein in particular has taken off.

The side effect: a price hike for whey protein concentrates as much as fivefold as demand sharply increased in the past few years, as we reported. In other words, whey protein powders are more expensive than ever.

So which ones are actually worth the steep price tag? To find out, we put 10 powders through rounds of testing. While many of our testers had less-than-thrilled reactions, comparing them to “watery coffee grounds” and calling them “Pepto Bismol-ish”, they weren’t all bad.

After a blind taste test in the Guardian’s New York office and a round of testing in our homes, a few stood out for their blend of convenience, nutritional content and least awful flavor – and one brand was unanimously crowned the winner.
points: Whey protein powder is everywhere, but which ones will you savor and which will you choke down?

articles.title: The kindness of strangers: In one of my darkest periods, a few compassionate words helped turn my life around
articles.summary: I was standing at the traffic lights with the weight of the world on my shoulders when a man approached. He will probably never know the impact he had on my life. My cousin had recently died in a terrible accident and I had been the one who had to identify the body.
body: One morning during rush hour, I stood at the traffic lights waiting to cross on my way to the office. I was lost in my thoughts but must have looked like I had the weight of the world on my shoulders, because something unexpected happened.
A man walked up, put his arm around me and said, “Everything is going to be OK.” I burst into tears and by the time I’d pulled myself together he was gone, disappeared into the crowd.
There was nothing remarkable about him at all. In fact, I can’t even remember his face. But that brief moment shifted everything for me.
I had been dwelling in victimhood and this stranger snapped me out of it. His kindness gave me enough hope to make a change and turn my life around.

He will probably never know the impact he had on my life.

articles.title: The Canned Vegetable That Transforms Creamy Pasta into a Comfort Meal
articles.summary: I have seen a lot of canned vegetable upgrades lately. One person suggested adding canned mushrooms to a grilled cheese, and another said to pour canned collard greens over white rice.
body: Food Editor Patty Catalano recommends adding creamed corn to chicken pot pie, enchiladas, corn chowder, and chili to make the dishes creamier. Senior Recipe Editor Christine Gallary likes to add a can to egg drop soup. Senior Culinary Producer Rachel Perlmutter adds it to corn chowder to make it creamier without adding more dairy. But what I was really interested in was adding a can to Alfredo sauce. So I followed our recipe for the best-ever fettuccine Alfredo with a slight twist. Here’s how it turned out.

Who knew my favorite ingredient in a fettuccine Alfredo was one day going to be a can of creamed corn? Well, it is now. An Alfredo sauce is obviously already very creamy. The main ingredients, after all, are Parmesan cheese, Pecorino Romano, heavy cream, and butter. They melt together into cheesy, creamy perfection, which can sometimes be a bit heavy. Adding a can of creamed corn helps to cut some of that richness.

articles.title: Where to Stay in the Pacific Northwest for a Coastal Fall Getaway
articles.summary: Whether it’s a remote cabin tucked between towering Douglas-firs, or a historic Queen Anne farmhouse in Portland, the Pacific Northwest is the perfect fall getaway—here's where to stay.
body: Chalk it up to my obsession with Twin Peaks, affinity for mossy landscapes, and lifelong fascination with all things misty and mystic; the Pacific Northwest has always felt like a second home. So much so, in fact, that I chose the region for my wedding back in 2024. More recently, I penned a love letter to one of its islands in honor of Practical Magic, and a travel guide to its most famous wine country, the Willamette Valley. The forests are vast, the food is mind-blowing, and the pace is delectably slow—it’s an all-around perfect travel destination, really.

While summers in the Pacific Northwest are characterized by exhilarating mountain summits and paddling along coastal waters, it’s equally appealing in autumn. To state the obvious, the foliage this time of year is downright show-stopping. Plus, you can still hike trails in national parks like the Cascades and Mt. Rainier (and with fewer crowds to boot). Go for a scenic drive, pop into an orchard for a cider tasting, and conclude your day in front of a crackling fireplace. The dream!

articles.title: From the Archives: American Great, Lee Krasner
articles.summary: “American Great: Lee Krasner,” by Barbara Rose, was originally published in the June 1972 issue of Vogue.
body: Although much curiosity, much speculation surround the formidable personality of Lee Pollock, the widow of the great American painter, very little is known about Lee Krasner, the artist who fought the same battles, exhibited in the same galleries, and painted side by side with her famous, now legendary, husband. For me, as well as many other critics, Lee Krasner is one of the significant painters of the twentieth century—an artist whose importance is only now beginning to be seen.

When I asked Lee Krasner why she was not one of the “Irascible Eighteen,” the now famous group of New York School artists who signed a petition in the ’forties—precipitating one of the most notable controversies ever stirred up about American painting—a petition protesting the virtual absence of American art in The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, she answered, “I wasn’t asked to sign. Barney Newman [the organizer of the protest, Barnett Newman, the outstanding American painter who died in 1970] called, and when I answered the phone, he asked for Jackson. He didn’t even bother to inform me of the protest.”
points: “American Great: Lee Krasner,” by Barbara Rose, was originally published in the June 1972 issue of Vogue.

articles.title: This IKEA Holiday Decoration Doubles as a Year-Round Entryway Organizer
articles.summary: Even though it seems like summer just ended, the holidays are closer than ever. If you’re the type of person who loves decking their home out in all sorts of festive adornments, you’re probably thrilled.
body: Fear not: IKEA just came out with a practical, minimalist “Christmas tree” that’s festive yet easy to love year-round. Say hello to the VINTERFINT wall decoration, which doubles as an entryway organizer.

Made of solid pine, the wall decoration is essentially a pegboard-style wall organizer in the shape of a Christmas tree. But unlike a heavy real Christmas tree (or bulky faux tree that comes in pieces), the VINTERFINT’s “flexible construction is easy to pull horizontally to the desired width and fill with decorations — and to fold up and store.” If I wasn’t already won over by this charmingly minimalist decor, I am now.

Although IKEA calls this an “alternative Christmas tree” (and you should certainly use it as such), this wall decoration’s geometric design, neutral color palette, and pegs means that you could keep it up year-round as an entryway or wall organizer, without looking like one of those people who can’t accept that Christmas comes but once a year.

articles.title: Lady Gaga Does New-Mom Dressing in a Very Lady Gaga Way
articles.summary: The singer is still devoted to her signature sky-high shoes.
body: This fall, Lady Gaga has gently set aside pop superstardom for the busy life of a new mom; the singer and her fiancé, Michael Polansky, welcomed a child together —a daughter named Rose Bean Polansky—in September.

Sure, there will likely be, sadly but understandably, no new Gaga album or tour in the immediate future—but that doesn’t mean her personal style is going anywhere. The proof? This weekend, Gaga was spotted leaving a hair salon in the Bay Area in one of her signature accessories: a sky-high pair of shoes.

Yet there were hints at a more practical approach to dressing in her errand outfit, too: Gaga went classic in jeans and a faded black tee, topping them off with a black knit cardigan cape and sunglasses. She also carried an XXL tote bag—presumably filled with all of baby Rose’s essentials.
But if Gaga is going to do one thing, it’s remain devoted to a killer shoe. After all, this is the star who once said she would “rather die than have my fans see me without a pair of heels on.”

articles.title: Apple Bread
articles.summary: Fresh chunks of apple + applesauce = double the fall flavor.
body: I’ve thought about that apple bread often, especially because I love making quick breads like pumpkin bread and banana bread. So I finally developed my own version. It lives up to the nostalgic memory of those Midwest fall road trips, with a blend of warm autumnal spices and chunks of apples in each bite.
Leftovers can be covered under a cake dome or tightly wrapped in plastic wrap and stored at room temperature for up to 4 days. I don’t recommend refrigerating it, which can dry the bread out faster.

Heat an oven to 350°F. Coat a 9x5-inch loaf pan with melted butter or cooking spray. Line the bottom and two long sides of the pan with a sheet of parchment paper that hangs over the edges by a few inches to form a sling.
Gently toss 1 1/2 cups peeled and diced large apple, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon together in a medium bowl.

articles.title: She Kept the Bathroom's 1950s Pink Tile — 1 DIY Made It Feel Brand New
articles.summary: Even if you have an extremely dated space, it doesn’t always require a total demo to look new and stylish again. Take Geneva Slye’s (@just.geneva) bathroom, for example. “The first thing you notice about the bathroom is the pink tile,” Geneva says.
body: Also part of the bathroom upon move-in? Gray peel-and-stick floor tiles, a newly installed toilet and sink, chrome light fixtures, and a silver-bordered mirror, all of which created a pink and gray color scheme that Geneva “immediately did not like.” Her goal “was not to do a full gut and remodel but to keep the tile because it was original, and to save money by keeping the new toilet and sink.”
“I knew it was something I could get creative with,” Geneva says. Her total redo cost $750.

Looking for a quick way to make your bathroom feel a bit more crisp and clean? Start by removing old, dirty caulk and re-caulking everything. That’s what Geneva did with her wall tile, and she says it made a huge difference. “I got all of the grout removed in a few hours one day and the new grout in on another day,” she says. “That also took only a few hours!”

Geneva also swapped the gray border tile she disliked for chair molding from Wayfair that she painted green ( Benjamin Moore’s “Turtle Green” ). Her final tile upgrade was replacing the peel-and-stick on the floors with the real deal (small hexagon tiles that came in 12×12-inch mesh sheets) — a first-time DIY project for her and her fiancé, Kevin.
points: Even if you have an extremely dated space, it doesn’t always require a total demo to look new and stylish again.
